first_impression.reaction: Googled '12 month wedding checklist' on the train. Intro is short and says it's month by month, good. But the Key Takeaways are mostly Australian paperwork and passports, not 'here's what to do each month'. I'd scroll for the month headings, find the at-a-glance table near the bottom, screenshot it and bookmark. Not enquiring.

journey.quote: This 12 month wedding checklist runs month by month, from the first decisions to the week of the wedding.
journey.reaction: Exactly what I searched for. Tells me the format straight away.

journey.quote: Your Notice of Intended Marriage must reach your authorised celebrant at least 1 month and no more than 18 months before the wedding.
journey.reaction: I'm in Singapore. What's a Notice of Intended Marriage? Three of four takeaways are legal and travel admin. I wanted a quick 'month 12 do this, month 6 do that'.

journey.section: How does a 12 month checklist change for a destination wedding?
journey.quote: A wedding at home and a wedding abroad share most of the same decisions. What changes is the order.
journey.reaction: Another section before the actual list starts. I'd scroll past this.

journey.quote: Settle what you will spend, a rough guest count and the style of wedding before you look at a single venue, because those three choices shape everything else.
journey.reaction: Fine, but the 12 months out block itself is clear. Short bullets, easy on my phone.

journey.quote: Check both passports now. Allow at least 6 weeks from lodging an application to receiving a new passport, and the same for renewals.
journey.reaction: Good tip in principle, but this is Australian passport timing. Is it the same for me? The page doesn't say who it's for.

journey.quote: As at November 2026, the NOIM can be witnessed in person or remotely via audio-visual link.
journey.reaction: Nice that it's dated, so I know it's current. Just not relevant to me.

journey.quote: A Wedded Advisor is the one person who plans with you from start to finish, works in your time zone and agrees the fee in writing before any work begins.
journey.reaction: Mid-list sales bit. Short enough that I don't mind, but I'm not clicking. Works in my time zone is interesting though.

journey.quote: Send invitations once the venue, times and dress code are settled. For a destination wedding, send them early enough that guests can still book flights and leave.
journey.reaction: 'Early enough' isn't an answer. How many weeks? The heading promised 'when to send wedding invitations'.

journey.section: Your 12 month wedding checklist at a glance
journey.quote: Print this table and keep it with your planning notes.
journey.reaction: This is the bit I actually wanted. Screenshot. It should be near the top, not after ten sections.

journey.section: Your 12 month wedding checklist at a glance
journey.quote: For a printable version alongside real weddings and destination ideas, sign up for the [Wedded Wonderland magazine]
journey.reaction: So the printable needs a sign-up. Slightly annoying, but the table is right there so I'll just screenshot.

journey.quote: Yes. Start with the 10 to 11 months out block and fold the 12 month tasks into your first few weeks
journey.reaction: Direct yes and a practical how. Good FAQ.

unanswered_questions: How many weeks before the wedding should invitations and save-the-dates go out?
Does the legal and passport advice apply if I'm not Australian (e.g. in Singapore)?
Can I download the printable version without signing up to the magazine?
Does Wedded Concierge work with couples outside Australia, and what does it cost? (deferred business detail)

turn_offs_found.quote: Your Notice of Intended Marriage must reach your authorised celebrant at least 1 month and no more than 18 months before the wedding.
turn_offs_found.why: Key Takeaways lead with Australian legal admin instead of a month-by-month summary, so the answer to my search isn't in the first 100 words, and a non-Australian reader doesn't know what this is.

turn_offs_found.quote: A wedding at home and a wedding abroad share most of the same decisions. What changes is the order.
turn_offs_found.why: An extra explainer section sits between the takeaways and the first month, so the actual checklist is buried below more intro.

turn_offs_found.quote: For a destination wedding, send them early enough that guests can still book flights and leave.
turn_offs_found.why: The heading 'when to send wedding invitations' matches my question but the section never gives a timeframe.

would_share_with: My fiancé and my mum: a screenshot of the at-a-glance table

cta_reaction.quote: When you are ready, [talk to Wedded Concierge] about your date and destination.
cta_reaction.why: I came for a checklist and don't know the brand. Nothing says whether they work with people outside Australia or what it costs. Bookmark, not enquire.

top_3_changes: Move the at-a-glance table (or a short version) up into or just after the Key Takeaways so the month-by-month answer is visible in the first screen.
Rewrite the Key Takeaways as a month-by-month summary, and label the Australian legal points as 'if marrying in Australia'.
Give an actual timeframe for save-the-dates and invitations in the '4 to 5 months out: when to send wedding invitations' section.
